```{r load}
# data from data-raw/temperature_vignette_data.R and data-raw/temperature_vignette_map.R
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
v <- readRDS(vd("temperature_values.rds"))
map <- readRDS(vd("temperature_map.rds"))
net <- attr(map, "network")
nodes <- utils::read.csv(vd("temperature_chain_nodes.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
edges <- utils::read.csv(vd("temperature_chain_edges.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = character())
prov <- v$provenance
pick <- v$pick
# the two bundles were built from one set of stations
stopifnot(identical(map$stations$station_number, v$stations$station_number),
          identical(map$stations$station_number[map$stations$picked], pick$station_number))

# colours come from the gq registries, so no hex literal appears in this article;
# assert each class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_temperature.csv", package = "wet"))
reg_main <- gq::gq_reg_main()
classes <- function(layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(reg$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_year <- classes("temperature_year", c("observed", "filled", "interval", "open_loop", "season"))
pal_map <- classes("temperature_map", c("basin", "network", "river", "station", "station_pick"))
pal_chain <- classes("temperature_chain", c("in_place", "building", "network_model", "comparison"))
pal_hold <- classes("temperature_holdout", c("hidden", "used", "unused", "stream", "lean"))
lake_sty <- reg_main$layers$lake
town_sty <- reg_main$layers$town
ink <- "grey35"   # frames, arrows and outlines: not a data colour

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
num <- function(x, digits = 0) format(round(x, digits), big.mark = ",", nsmall = digits, trim = TRUE)
day_text <- function(d) paste(as.integer(format(d, "%d")), format(d, "%B"))
and_text <- function(x) sub(", ([^,]*)$", " and \\1", paste(x, collapse = ", "))
compass <- function(dx, dy) {
  c("east", "north-east", "north", "north-west", "west", "south-west", "south",
    "south-east")[(round(atan2(dy, dx) / (pi / 4)) %% 8) + 1]
}
to_title <- function(x) {
  vapply(strsplit(tolower(x), " "), function(w) {
    big <- !w %in% c("at", "the", "near", "of", "in", "below")
    w[big] <- paste0(toupper(substring(w[big], 1, 1)), substring(w[big], 2))
    paste(w, collapse = " ")
  }, "")
}
```

```{r year-data}
yr <- v$year
season <- v$season
# the prose says "the season" and the recipe types the station and the year
stopifnot(nrow(season) == 1, identical(pick$station_number, "08EE012"), pick$year == 2020L,
          identical(pick$stream, "Simpson Creek"))
year_text <- pick$year
in_win <- yr$date >= as.Date(paste0(pick$year, "-03-01")) & yr$date <= as.Date(paste0(pick$year, "-11-30"))
in_gap <- yr$date >= pick$gap_start & yr$date <= pick$gap_end
in_season <- yr$date >= season$start & yr$date <= season$end
# "every day from March through November except the gap": the filled days of the window are the gap
stopifnot(identical(yr$filled[in_win], in_gap[in_win]), sum(in_gap) == pick$gap_days)
# degree days add up over the season to the bundled total; without the fill there is none
yr$dd <- NA_real_
yr$dd[in_season] <- cumsum(yr$t_mean_c[in_season])
gsdd <- v$gsdd$filled
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(max(yr$dd, na.rm = TRUE), gsdd)), is.na(v$gsdd$unfilled),
          season$start <= pick$gap_start, season$end >= pick$gap_end)
# the worked example in the prose: 100 days at 10 degrees
stopifnot(100 * 10 == 1000)
# the last reading before the gap: warmer than the day before although the air was not
edge <- v$edge
air_at <- function(d) yr$air_c[yr$date == d]
jump <- edge$t_mean_c - edge$t_before_c
stopifnot(edge$date == pick$gap_start - 1, jump > 5, air_at(edge$date) - air_at(edge$date - 1) >= 0, air_at(edge$date) - air_at(edge$date - 1) < 0.5,
          edge$t_mean_c - air_at(edge$date) > 5)
edge_cost <- gsdd - edge$gsdd
stopifnot(edge_cost > 50, edge_cost < 100)
# open-loop runs cooler than the fill across the gap
stopifnot(edge$gap_open < edge$gap_edge, edge$gap_edge < edge$gap_filled)

# where the stream is: what it flows into, and the town it is nearest
st_xy <- sf::st_coordinates(map$stations)
pl_xy <- sf::st_coordinates(map$places)
p <- which(map$stations$picked)
d_town <- sqrt((pl_xy[, 1] - st_xy[p, 1])^2 + (pl_xy[, 2] - st_xy[p, 2])^2) / 1000
near <- which.min(d_town)
town_near <- map$places$name[near]
town_km <- round(d_town[near])
town_dir <- compass(st_xy[p, 1] - pl_xy[near, 1], st_xy[p, 2] - pl_xy[near, 2])
stopifnot(identical(town_near, "Smithers"), town_km <= 10, identical(pick$into1, "Kathlyn Creek"),
          identical(pick$into2, "Bulkley River"))
# "at a few hundred stations": the stations the fill was validated at
stopifnot(v$validation$truth_stations >= 200, v$validation$truth_stations < 500)

# figure 1, in two panels on one time axis
panels <- c(temp = "Water temperature (°C)", dd = "Degree days so far")
runs <- function(keep) {
  x <- yr[keep & !is.na(yr$t_mean_c), ]
  x$run <- cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(as.integer(x$date)) > 1))
  x
}
panel <- function(x, k) {
  x$panel <- factor(panels[[k]], panels)
  x
}
obs <- panel(runs(!yr$filled %in% TRUE), "temp")
fil <- panel(runs(yr$filled %in% TRUE), "temp")
open <- panel(yr[!is.na(yr$s_open_c), ], "temp")
band <- rbind(panel(season, "temp"), panel(season, "dd"))
dd <- panel(yr[in_season, ], "dd")
dd_fill <- panel(yr[in_season & (in_gap | yr$date == pick$gap_start - 1), ], "dd")
total <- panel(data.frame(date = season$end, dd = gsdd, label = paste(num(gsdd), "degree days")), "dd")
level_text <- "95%"   # wet_temp_fill()'s default interval
stopifnot(formals(wet_temp_fill)$level == 0.95)

cap_year <- sprintf(paste(
  "%s at its mouth in %s. Top: each day's mean water temperature as the station recorded it (black);",
  "the %s days filled across the gap from %s to %s (orange), with the fill's %s interval (pale band);",
  "and what air temperature alone gives through air2stream, the open-loop line (blue). Bottom: degree",
  "days adding up through the growing season, %s to %s (shaded in both panels), to %s; the stretch",
  "that rests on filled days is orange. The last reading before the gap, %s °C after %s °C the day",
  "before, is most likely a sensor leaving the water, and the fill starts from it."
), pick$stream, year_text, pick$gap_days, day_text(pick$gap_start), day_text(pick$gap_end), level_text,
day_text(season$start), day_text(season$end), num(gsdd), num(edge$t_mean_c, 1), num(edge$t_before_c, 1))
alt_year <- sprintf(paste(
  "Two stacked charts of %s in %s. The top chart shows daily water temperature rising from near zero",
  "in winter to a summer peak, with a gap in late August and September filled by a modelled line, and",
  "a second line for what air temperature alone predicts.",
  "The bottom chart shows degree days climbing to %s by the end of the growing season."
), pick$stream, year_text, num(gsdd))
```

**The R package [`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/), for stream flow and water temperature
in British Columbia, does not yet give temperature for every stream reach** [@wet]. This article shows where that work starts, what it aims for, and how
it will be tested. The aim is growing-season degree days, a measure of how much warmth a
stream gives young fish in a year, at every reach (a mapped stretch of stream) in British Columbia. Today
they can be computed at a few hundred stations across the province. Getting from those to every reach
takes a model on the stream network.
[The roadmap](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/issues/214) says what is done and what is next.

## What are growing-season degree days, and why do they matter for fish?

A fish grows faster in warmer water. **Growing-season degree days** add up that warmth
over the part of the year when a stream is warm enough for growth: each day's mean water temperature,
summed from the first week that averages above 5 °C to the first week that falls below 4 °C
[@coleman_fausch2007ColdSummera]. A stream that holds 10 °C for 100 days gives 1,000 degree days. Where
the total is low, fish that hatch in summer can be too small to survive their first winter
[@coleman_fausch2007ColdSummera], so the total helps say which streams can produce fish.

The figure shows one year at one station: `r pick$stream` at its mouth, about `r town_km` km `r town_dir`
of `r town_near`, where it joins `r pick$into1` on the way to the `r pick$into2`. The station recorded every day from March through November
of `r year_text` except `r pick$gap_days` days from `r day_text(pick$gap_start)`. A season with a
missing day has no total, so the gap is filled first.
[`wet_temp_fill()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/reference/wet_temp_fill.html) fills it with
**air2stream**, a model of how water temperature follows air temperature [@toffolon_piccolroaz2015hybridmodel],
corrected by the station's own readings on either side of the gap and by what nearby stations did on
the same days. Run on air temperature alone, with no readings to correct it, the model is called
**open-loop**. A reach with no station has no readings, so open-loop is where it starts.

```{r year, fig.height = 5.6, fig.cap = cap_year, fig.alt = alt_year}
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = band, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "season")) +
  geom_ribbon(data = fil, aes(date, ymin = t_lo_c, ymax = t_hi_c, group = run, fill = "interval")) +
  geom_line(data = open, aes(date, s_open_c, colour = "open_loop"), linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_line(data = obs, aes(date, t_mean_c, group = run, colour = "observed"), linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_line(data = fil, aes(date, t_mean_c, group = run, colour = "filled"), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = dd, aes(date, dd, colour = "observed"), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = dd_fill, aes(date, dd, colour = "filled"), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = total, aes(date, dd, label = label), hjust = -0.08, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.2) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ ., scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_year$values[c("observed", "filled", "open_loop")],
                      labels = pal_year$labels[c("observed", "filled", "open_loop")],
                      breaks = c("observed", "filled", "open_loop"), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_year$values[c("interval", "season")],
                    labels = pal_year$labels[c("interval", "season")], breaks = c("interval", "season"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b", expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1), fill = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 9.5),
        legend.box = "vertical", legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

The fill restarts from every reading, so a bad one is carried into it. Here the last reading before
the gap is about `r num(jump)` °C above the day before while the air barely warmed. The
figure shows the year as the method gives it; hiding that one reading lowers the total from
`r num(gsdd)` to `r num(edge$gsdd)` degree days.

## Where do we have temperature, and where not?

```{r map-data}
bb <- sf::st_bbox(map$extent)
lim_x <- c(bb[["xmin"]], bb[["xmax"]])
lim_y <- c(bb[["ymin"]], bb[["ymax"]])
dx <- diff(lim_x)
dy <- diff(lim_y)
map_w <- 7
map_h <- map_w * dy / dx

n_reach <- net$reaches
n_st <- nrow(map$stations)
# every order of the network is drawn, and each station holds a reach of its own
stopifnot(all(net$orders$drawn), net$with_station == n_st, n_reach == sum(net$orders$segments))
# the prose gives sizes, not counts that move: "tens of thousands of reaches", "about a dozen" stations
stopifnot(n_reach >= 2e4, n_reach < 1e5, n_st >= 9, n_st <= 15)
# "most reaches are small streams and few stations sit on one, as in the basin above":
# small is stream order 1 or 2
share_small <- sum(net$orders$segments[net$orders$stream_order <= 2]) / n_reach
on_small <- mean(v$stations$stream_order <= 2)
stopifnot(share_small > 0.5, on_small < 0.25)
# the count is of stations with a day of record in the fixed range the data script reads
stopifnot(all(v$stations$days > 0), identical(substr(prov$to, 1, 4), "2025"))
last_year <- substr(prov$to, 1, 4)
# "some only recently": more than one station began in the last year read, too short to model yet
n_short <- sum(!map$stations$fitted)
stopifnot(n_short >= 2, n_short < n_st, all(format(v$stations$first[!v$stations$fitted], "%Y") == last_year))

# the rivers named, and the towns: the Bulkley runs from Houston to the Skeena at Hazelton
rivers <- map$streams[map$streams$main, ]
stopifnot(setequal(rivers$gnis_name, c("Bulkley River", "Morice River", "Telkwa River")))
skeena <- map$streams[map$streams$gnis_name %in% "Skeena River", ]
bulkley <- rivers[rivers$gnis_name == "Bulkley River", ]
town <- function(n) pl_xy[map$places$name == n, ]
stopifnot(nrow(skeena) == 1, as.numeric(sf::st_distance(bulkley, skeena)) < 500,
          setequal(map$places$name, c("Houston", "Smithers", "Hazelton")))
# Hazelton is where the two rivers meet: the town lies within 5 km of the Skeena and of the Bulkley
hz <- map$places[map$places$name == "Hazelton", ]
stopifnot(as.numeric(sf::st_distance(hz, skeena)) < 5000, as.numeric(sf::st_distance(hz, bulkley)) < 5000)
flow_dir <- compass(town("Hazelton")[1] - town("Houston")[1], town("Hazelton")[2] - town("Houston")[2])
# Smithers lies between them along the river: nearer each than they are to one another
gap_km <- function(a, b) sqrt(sum((town(a) - town(b))^2)) / 1000
stopifnot(gap_km("Houston", "Smithers") < gap_km("Houston", "Hazelton"),
          gap_km("Smithers", "Hazelton") < gap_km("Houston", "Hazelton"))

# labels: towns, rivers (at a point on each line inside the frame) and the first figure's station
frame <- sf::st_as_sfc(bb)
on_line <- function(x) {
  inside <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_intersection(sf::st_geometry(x), frame))
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_cast(inside, "POINT"))
  xy[ceiling(nrow(xy) / 2), 1:2]
}
named <- rbind(rivers[c("gnis_name")], skeena[c("gnis_name")])
riv_xy <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(named)), function(i) on_line(named[i, ]), c(0, 0)))
lab <- rbind(
  data.frame(x = pl_xy[, 1], y = pl_xy[, 2], label = map$places$name, face = "bold", size = 3.4,
             col = town_sty$label$color),
  data.frame(x = riv_xy[, 1], y = riv_xy[, 2], label = named$gnis_name, face = "italic", size = 3.1,
             col = lake_sty$label$color),
  data.frame(x = st_xy[p, 1], y = st_xy[p, 2], label = pick$stream, face = "plain", size = 3.1, col = "black"),
  # the other stations carry no label, but every label keeps clear of them
  data.frame(x = st_xy[-p, 1], y = st_xy[-p, 2], label = "", face = "plain", size = 3.1, col = "black")
)

# scale bar in the lower left, its length from gq
sb_km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(bb))
sb <- data.frame(x = lim_x[1] + 0.05 * dx, y = lim_y[1] + 0.035 * dy)
sb$xend <- sb$x + sb_km * 1000

# keymap: BC with the map extent, in the lower right
key <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = map$bc, fill = "white", colour = ink, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = frame, fill = NA, colour = pal_map$values[["station"]], linewidth = 0.6) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = ink, linewidth = 0.3))
key_w <- 0.27 * dx
key_h <- key_w * 1.05

stations <- map$stations
stations$part <- ifelse(stations$picked, "station_pick", "station")
stations <- stations[order(stations$picked), ]
tree <- map$tree
tree$part <- "network"
rivers$part <- "river"
# what the map script drew, as the bundle records it; a lake cut by the frame keeps its whole area
drawn <- attr(map, "drawn")
lake_min <- drawn$lake_min_ha
stopifnot(identical(lake_min, 500), identical(drawn$context_min_order, 7), min(map$lakes$area_ha) >= lake_min,
          all(map$streams$stream_order[!map$streams$main] >= drawn$context_min_order))

cap_map <- sprintf(paste(
  "One basin as an example, the %s: every reach of its stream network (blue, heavier on larger streams) and the federal",
  "hydrometric stations that have recorded water temperature (orange points; %s's, the first figure's,",
  "is black).",
  "The %s are drawn heavy and named. Lakes of %s ha and up are pale blue; land outside the basin is",
  "dimmed, with its larger rivers thin and the Skeena named. %s are labelled (open squares), the bar is",
  "%s km, and the inset places the map in British Columbia."
), v$basin$name, pick$stream,
and_text(sub(" River", "", c("Bulkley River", "Morice River", "Telkwa River"))) |> paste("rivers"),
lake_min, and_text(c("Houston", "Smithers", "Hazelton")), sb_km)
alt_map <- sprintf(paste(
  "Map of the %s basin in north-west British Columbia, densely covered by thin blue stream lines,",
  "with about a dozen orange and black points marking temperature stations on its rivers and creeks."
), v$basin$name)
```

The aim is the whole province; the `r v$basin$name` basin is used here only as an example. A **reach** here is one stream segment of the Freshwater Atlas, the province's
map of its streams [@flnrord2021FreshwaterAtlasb]. The `r v$basin$name` runs `r flow_dir` from Houston past Smithers to meet the
Skeena River at Hazelton, and the stream network of its basin has tens of thousands of reaches. About a
dozen hold a federal hydrometric station that has recorded water temperature, some only recently.
Small-stream loggers are not in `wet` yet.

```{r map, fig.width = map_w, fig.height = map_h, fig.cap = cap_map, fig.alt = alt_map}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = map$extent, fill = "grey88", colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = map$basin, fill = pal_map$values[["basin"]], colour = ink, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = tree, aes(linewidth = stream_order, colour = part), key_glyph = "path") +
  geom_sf(data = map$lakes, fill = lake_sty$fill$color, colour = lake_sty$stroke$color, linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = map$streams[!map$streams$main, ], colour = pal_map$values[["river"]], linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = rivers, aes(colour = part), linewidth = 0.95, key_glyph = "path") +
  geom_sf(data = stations, aes(fill = part), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 3, stroke = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = map$places, shape = 0, colour = "black", size = 3.6, stroke = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(x, y, label = label, fontface = face, size = I(size), colour = I(col)),
                           bg.color = "white", bg.r = 0.18, seed = 1, point.padding = 3, box.padding = 0.5,
                           min.segment.length = Inf, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = sb, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = sb, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y, label = paste(sb_km, "km")), vjust = -0.7, size = 3.4) +
  annotation_custom(ggplotGrob(key), xmin = lim_x[2] - key_w - 0.02 * dx, xmax = lim_x[2] - 0.02 * dx,
                    ymin = lim_y[1] + 0.015 * dy, ymax = lim_y[1] + 0.015 * dy + key_h) +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.06, 0.75), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_map$values[c("network", "river")], labels = pal_map$labels[c("network", "river")],
                      breaks = c("network", "river"), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_map$values[c("station", "station_pick")],
                    labels = pal_map$labels[c("station", "station_pick")], breaks = c("station", "station_pick"),
                    name = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3)),
         colour = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(linewidth = c(0.4, 0.95)))) +
  coord_sf(xlim = lim_x, ylim = lim_y, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.985),
        legend.justification = c(1, 1), legend.box.just = "left", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        legend.margin = margin(3, 6, 3, 6), legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt"),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = ink))
```

The network drawn stands on Simon Norris's [`fwapg`](https://smnorris.github.io/fwapg/)
[@norris2024smnorrisfwapg], which loads the Freshwater Atlas into PostgreSQL. Side channels are trimmed
from it so that water never splits on its way downstream, as a stream network model needs; that step
runs from a fork of `fwapg` today [@norris_irvine2026NewGraphEnvironmentfwapg].

## How do we get from stations to every reach?

```{r chain-data}
states <- names(pal_chain$values)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(nodes$id), all(nodes$state %in% states), all(states %in% nodes$state),
          all(edges$from %in% nodes$id), all(edges$to %in% nodes$id), all(edges$style %in% c("solid", "dashed")))
# the chain ends where the article's title points: degree days at every reach, from a network model
ends <- setdiff(nodes$id, edges$from)
stopifnot(setequal(ends, c("gsdd_station", "gsdd_reach")),
          nodes$state[nodes$id == "gsdd_reach"] == "network_model",
          "model" %in% edges$from[edges$to == "gsdd_reach"])
# what feeds what, as the prose and the figure's alt text say it
feeds <- function(to) sort(edges$from[edges$to == to], method = "radix")
stopifnot(identical(feeds("fills"), c("air_station", "readings")),
          identical(feeds("baseline"), c("fills", "pcic", "traits")),
          identical(feeds("model"), c("air_reach", "baseline", "network")))
# the process model is the comparison, and only it is joined by dashed arrows
comp <- nodes$id[nodes$state == "comparison"]
stopifnot(identical(comp, "pcic"), identical(edges$style == "dashed", edges$from %in% comp))
nodes$label <- gsub("|", "\n", nodes$label, fixed = TRUE)
edges$label <- gsub("|", "\n", edges$label, fixed = TRUE)
nodes$hw <- 1.45                                                    # half a box's width
nodes$hh <- 0.12 + 0.17 * lengths(strsplit(nodes$label, "\n"))      # and of its height
nodes$state <- factor(nodes$state, states)
# each arrow runs between the two boxes' edges, along the line that joins their centres
a <- nodes[match(edges$from, nodes$id), ]
b <- nodes[match(edges$to, nodes$id), ]
ux <- b$x - a$x
uy <- b$y - a$y
out <- pmin(a$hw / abs(ux), a$hh / abs(uy))
into <- pmin(b$hw / abs(ux), b$hh / abs(uy))
arrows <- data.frame(x = a$x + out * ux, y = a$y + out * uy, xend = b$x - into * ux * 1.04,
                     yend = b$y - into * uy * 1.04, style = edges$style, label = edges$label)
arrows$mx <- (arrows$x + arrows$xend) / 2
arrows$my <- (arrows$y + arrows$yend) / 2
n_state <- table(nodes$state)

cap_chain <- paste(
  "From station readings to degree days at every reach. Each box is one piece and each arrow says what",
  "feeds what. The box's colour says where the piece stands: in place (green), being built (orange),",
  "what a network model would add (blue), and a process model that already exists (purple), joined by",
  "dashed arrows because it is a comparison and a source of future change, not a step in the chain."
)
alt_chain <- paste(
  "Flow diagram. Station readings and air temperature feed gap filling; filled records and catchment",
  "traits feed a baseline; the baseline, the stream network and air temperature at every reach feed a",
  "network model, which gives degree days at every reach. A process model sits to one side."
)
```

The diagram shows how readings at a few stations become a value everywhere; its colours say which
parts exist.

```{r chain, fig.height = 6.2, fig.cap = cap_chain, fig.alt = alt_chain}
ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = arrows, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend, linetype = style), colour = ink,
               linewidth = 0.45, arrow = arrow(length = unit(5, "pt"), type = "closed"), show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_rect(data = nodes, aes(xmin = x - hw, xmax = x + hw, ymin = y - hh, ymax = y + hh, colour = state,
                              fill = state), linewidth = 0.9, key_glyph = "rect") +
  geom_text(data = nodes, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 2.95, lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_label(data = arrows[nzchar(arrows$label), ], aes(mx, my, label = label), size = 2.6, colour = ink,
             fill = "white", linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt"), lineheight = 0.9,
             fontface = "italic") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_chain$values, labels = pal_chain$labels, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = alpha(pal_chain$values, 0.14), labels = pal_chain$labels, name = NULL,
                    drop = FALSE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(solid = "solid", dashed = "22")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.15, 10.15), ylim = c(0.3, 10.1), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(4, 0, 0, 0))
```

- **Catchment traits** describe the land above a point: its position, elevation, snow, lakes and
  glaciers.
- **The baseline** is the simple answer: what catchment traits alone can say. air2stream has three settings
  that say how closely a stream's water follows the air, fitted at each station. The baseline predicts
  them where there is no station from catchment traits, two ways: by a relation fitted across
  stations, or from the stations most like it.
- **A network model** fits every station at once and lets reaches on the same stream inform each
  other. It can draw on everything above it in the diagram: the network, the stations and their filled
  records, the traits, air temperature at every reach, and how the baseline did. What is needed from it
  is temperature at every reach with its uncertainty, and degree days with that uncertainty carried
  through. Network models of weekly stream temperature have been fitted for the Nechako and Skeena
  watersheds [@hill_etal2024Spatialstream; @hill_etal2025Spatialstream], and this work follows them. The
  method and the time step are open.

A **process model** works the other way, simulating water and heat moving down rivers from the weather.
The Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium's model [@pacificclimateimpactsconsortium2026VICGLRavenMBCn]
gives daily water temperature at points on its own river network, on past weather and under climate
models to 2100. Its temperatures can be compared with the same station records, and it is one way to
ask where streams are becoming warm enough for fish.

## How will it be tested?

```{r holdout-data}
# a toy network: streams as lines, stations as points; `h` is the station hidden
stream <- function(id, x, y) data.frame(id = id, x = x, y = y)
toy <- rbind(stream("main", c(5, 5, 4.5, 5), c(0, 3, 6, 9.6)),
             stream("west", c(5, 2.5, 1), c(3, 4.5, 7)),
             stream("west_fork", c(2.5, 2.2), c(4.5, 7.6)),
             stream("east_upper", c(4.5, 7, 8.5), c(6, 7, 9)),
             stream("east_lower", c(5, 7.5, 9), c(1.5, 2.5, 4.6)))
sites <- data.frame(id = c("h", "a", "f", "b", "c", "d", "e"),
                    x = c(3.4, 1.4, 2.25, 5, 4.7, 7.6, 8.2),
                    y = c(3.96, 6.33, 7.1, 2.2, 7.4, 7.8, 3.48))
ways <- c(traits = "From catchment traits", like = "From the stations most like it",
          network = "From traits and the stream network")
# the network's prediction keeps the traits, so it draws on every other station, and leans most
# on the stream that runs up and down from the hidden one (drawn heavy)
use <- list(traits = setdiff(sites$id, "h"), like = c("a", "d", "e"), network = setdiff(sites$id, "h"))
lean <- rbind(toy[toy$id %in% c("west", "west_fork"), ], stream("main_below", c(5, 5), c(0, 3)))
lean$way <- factor(ways[["network"]], ways)
# each way draws on other stations only; the middle one on fewer than the others
stopifnot(!"h" %in% unlist(use), all(unlist(use) %in% sites$id), length(use$like) < length(use$traits),
          setequal(use$traits, use$network))
hold <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ways), function(k) {
  s <- sites
  s$part <- ifelse(s$id == "h", "hidden", ifelse(s$id %in% use[[k]], "used", "unused"))
  s$way <- factor(ways[[k]], ways)
  s
}))
hold$part <- factor(hold$part, c("hidden", "used", "unused"))
toy_way <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ways, function(w) cbind(toy, way = factor(w, ways))))
# the station error "What is not known yet?" quotes: a whole season hidden, air temperature alone
val <- v$validation
season_mae <- val$season_open$gsdd_mae
stopifnot(season_mae > 100, season_mae < 150)

cap_hold <- paste(
  "The test, as a sketch on a made-up network (pale lines). One station is hidden (orange) and its",
  "air2stream settings are predicted three ways, each drawing on the stations in blue and leaving the",
  "grey ones out: from catchment traits, a relation fitted to every other station; from the few",
  "stations whose catchments are most like it, wherever they are; and from traits and the stream",
  "network together, leaning most on the stream that runs up and down from the hidden station (heavy",
  "line). The first two are the baseline."
)
alt_hold <- paste(
  "Three copies of a small branching stream network with seven stations. One station is marked as",
  "hidden in each; the stations used to predict it differ, and the third copy marks the stream",
  "through the hidden station."
)
```

By hiding stations. A **holdout** takes a station's whole record away, predicts it as if the station
had never been there, and compares the prediction with what the station recorded. Three simple
predictions are to be tested this way, at stations across the province with a complete growing season,
on daily temperature and the season's degree days: the baseline's two, and one that adds the stream
network. The same hidden stations are there for any model to be compared on.

```{r holdout, fig.height = 3, fig.cap = cap_hold, fig.alt = alt_hold}
ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = toy_way, aes(x, y, group = id, colour = "stream"), linewidth = 1.3, lineend = "round",
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_path(data = lean, aes(x, y, group = id, colour = "lean"), linewidth = 2.6, lineend = "round",
            key_glyph = "path") +
  geom_point(data = hold, aes(x, y, fill = part), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 3.6, stroke = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~way, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_hold$values[c("stream", "lean")], breaks = "lean",
                      labels = pal_hold$labels["lean"], name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_hold$values[c("hidden", "used", "unused")],
                    labels = pal_hold$labels[c("hidden", "used", "unused")], name = NULL) +
  # two legends: give each its place, or their order follows a hash that differs between sessions
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1), colour = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0.3, 9.7), ylim = c(-0.2, 9.9), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 9.5, margin = margin(0, 0, 4, 0)),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey80"), panel.spacing = unit(8, "pt"))
```

The third is **kriging**: estimating a value at an unmeasured place from measured places, weighting
the near ones most. On a stream network, near is measured along the water and in the direction it
flows. Here it is a simple stand-in for the network, not the network model: it adds the network to the
same traits, so its difference from the baseline is what the network adds. Each of the
three is then run through air2stream on the hidden station's own air temperature and compared with two
marks: the model fitted to that station's own record, the best these three could do, and the average
of all stations, what knowing nothing gives. Each
is tried twice, with and without the hidden station's neighbours up and down its stream; for the
network's prediction that difference is what the neighbours are worth.

## What is not known yet?

- **The error with no station.** Even at a station, when a whole growing season is hidden, air2stream
  on air temperature alone misses that season's total by about `r num(season_mae)` degree days on
  average. With air2stream, a reach with no station can only do worse; how much worse is what the test
  measures.
- **Small streams.** Most reaches are small streams and few stations sit on one, as in the basin above,
  so the test says least about them.
- **Readings that are not water.** Nothing screens yet for one like the first figure's.
- **The thresholds.** They exist for cutthroat trout in high-elevation
  Colorado streams, where 900 to 1,200 degree days gave the best recruitment and under 800 was
  unsuitable [@coleman_fausch2007ColdSummera]. Reports on westslope cutthroat trout in the Elk Valley
  apply them [@thorley_branton2022SubjectMatter; @hocking_etal2022SubjectMatter]. None has been found
  yet for other British Columbia species.

## How were the numbers in the first figure made?

The fill borrows from its sub-drainage's other stations, so the recipe reads them all.

```{r recipe, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(wet)

# the gauges of WSC sub-drainage 08E; most record no water temperature, and
# wet_temp_daily() warns of those and returns the ones that do
st <- tidyhydat::allstations
st <- st[startsWith(st$STATION_NUMBER, "08E"), ]
water <- wet_temp_daily(st$STATION_NUMBER, from = "2002-01-01", to = "2025-12-31")
st <- st[st$STATION_NUMBER %in% water$station_number, ]

# daily air temperature at each, then the fill and the degree days
air <- cd::cd_extract_daily(data.frame(id = st$STATION_NUMBER, lon = st$LONGITUDE, lat = st$LATITUDE),
                            "2002-01-01", "2025-12-31", variables = "tmean")
pool <- stats::setNames(substr(st$STATION_NUMBER, 1, 3), st$STATION_NUMBER)
filled <- wet_temp_fill(water, air, pool = pool)
gsdd <- wet_temp_gsdd(filled)
gsdd[gsdd$station_number == "08EE012" & gsdd$year == 2020, ]
```

```{r recipe-check}
# the recipe types the pool, the range and the pick; fail here if the bundle moves under it
stopifnot(identical(v$pool$prefix, "08E"), identical(prov$from, "2002-01-01"), identical(prov$to, "2025-12-31"))
```

## Software and citation

Water temperature was read from the archive on `r day_text(as.Date(prov$retrieved))`
`r format(as.Date(prov$retrieved), "%Y")`, for `r prov$from` to `r prov$to`; station coordinates and
areas are HYDAT's, release `r prov$hydat`; and the data were built at commit `r prov$commit`.

The software, each cited:

- [`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) [@wet] reads the station records, fills them and
  sums the degree days.
- [`cd`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/cd/) [@cd] serves daily air temperature at the stations.
- [`gsdd`](https://github.com/poissonconsulting/gsdd) [@gsdd] applies the growing-season rule, and
  [`tidyhydat`](https://docs.ropensci.org/tidyhydat/) [@tidyhydat] gives each station's time zone.
- [`fwapg`](https://smnorris.github.io/fwapg/) [@norris2024smnorrisfwapg] loads the Freshwater Atlas into
  PostgreSQL, and the network with no splits is built on it [@norris_irvine2026NewGraphEnvironmentfwapg].
  [`SSN2`](https://usepa.github.io/SSN2/) [@SSN2] is the software for kriging on a stream network.
- [`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) [@ggplot2], [`ggrepel`](https://ggrepel.slowkow.com/)
  [@ggrepel], [`gq`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/gq/) [@gq] and
  [`sf`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) [@sf] make the figures and the map;
  [`knitr`](https://yihui.org/knitr/) [@knitr] and [`bookdown`](https://pkgs.rstudio.com/bookdown/)
  [@bookdown] render the article, all in R [@base].

```{r versions, results = "asis"}
# our packages' version, and the commit where the install recorded a full git hash
# (a build from a checkout records none)
ours <- vapply(c("wet", "cd", "gq"), function(p) {
  sha <- utils::packageDescription(p)$RemoteSha
  sha <- if (!is.null(sha) && grepl("^[0-9a-f]{40}$", sha)) paste0(" (commit ", substr(sha, 1, 7), ")") else ""
  sprintf("`%s` %s%s", p, utils::packageVersion(p), sha)
}, "")
cat("This build ran on ", and_text(ours), "; the data were built with `cd` ", prov$cd, " and `gsdd` ",
    prov$gsdd, ". To cite `wet`:\n\n", sep = "")
cat(format(utils::citation("wet"), style = "text"), sep = "\n\n")
```

### Data

- Water temperature: Environment and Climate Change Canada's hydrometric stations
  [@environmentandclimatechangecanada2021NationalWater], as archived by
  [water-temp-bc](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/water-temp-bc)
  [@irvine2025NewGraphEnvironmentwatertempbc].
- Air temperature: ERA5-Land [@munoz-sabater_etal2021ERA5Landstateoftheart].
- The process model: the Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium's channel-scale output
  [@pacificclimateimpactsconsortium2026VICGLRavenMBCn], named here and not yet read by this article.
- Streams, lakes, the basin and place names: the Province of British Columbia's Freshwater Atlas
  [@flnrord2021FreshwaterAtlasb] and BC Geographic Names, through DataBC.

```{r wordcount, include = FALSE}
f <- knitr::current_input()
if (!is.null(f)) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  y <- utils::tail(x, -utils::head(which(x == "---"), 2)[2])   # drop the YAML header
  cite <- which(y == "## Software and citation")
  stopifnot(length(cite) == 1)
  y <- utils::head(y, cite - 1)   # the closing citation section is not body prose
  fence <- cumsum(grepl("^```", y)) %% 2 == 1
  y <- y[!fence & !grepl("^```", y)]
  y <- gsub("`r [^`]*`", "", y)          # inline code is not body prose
  y <- y[!grepl("^\\s*$", y)]
  n <- sum(lengths(strsplit(trimws(y), "\\s+")))
  message("body prose: ", n, " words")
  cap <- 1200   # set before the first draft was written
  if (n > cap) stop("body prose is ", n, " words; the cap is ", cap)
}
```
